heading: INT. NANA ROSALBA'S KITCHEN - POWER OUT - NIGHT

units.text: INT. NANA ROSALBA'S KITCHEN - POWER OUT - NIGHT
Candles in jam jars.
A pot of rice losing its heat on a dead stove.
Rain on the tin roof, loud as applause.
NANA ROSALBA, 80s, in a housecoat, ladles soup by feel.
Her son DESMOND, 50s, kneels at the breaker box with a phone flashlight in his teeth.
His daughter IMANI, 16, scrolls a dead phone in disgust.
KOFI, 9, hides under the table with a toy truck.
AUNT PETRA, 60s, wrings her hands by the window.
Everybody stay put.
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: We are staying put, Desmond, there is nowhere to go.
units.name: PETRA

units.text: Twelve percent. I had twelve percent.
units.name: IMANI

units.text: Bowls. Whoever is standing, get bowls.
units.name: NANA

units.text: It's too dark to find the bowls.
units.name: KOFI

units.text: Then find them with your hands, like Jesus.
units.name: NANA

units.text: Nana --
units.name: IMANI

units.text: Mama, he didn't --
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: It's in the Bible somewhere.
units.name: PETRA

units.text: Thunder cracks.
The candles gutter.
Kofi shrieks.
Everyone talks at once, and then all stop.
Nana places a bowl in front of her grandson, then touches his hair.
Eat.
units.name: NANA
